precepts.text: The dragon went to make war with the remnant of the woman's seed, those keeping the commandments of the Most High and holding the testimony of Jesus Christ; that remnant is the Israelites.
precepts.point: Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. The Most High will make a consumption decreed and overflowing with righteousness in the midst of all the land.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass in that day” is a future prophecy: “the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more again stay upon him that smote them; but shall stay upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.” Stay means to rely upon. Just like back then, we still rely upon the ones who smote us, even today under the nation of Edom, trusting in oppression, relying on the very ones still smiting us in the streets.

Revelation identifies that remnant: “the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” The remnant is the Israelites keeping the commandments of the Most High and holding the testimony of Jesus Christ. Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only that remnant, those keeping the commandments in their right mind, will escape and stop leaning on the oppressor.

precepts.text: For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return.
precepts.point: The remnant that possesses these things is named in the prophets, and it is the children of Israel. This is why the bible must be read precept upon precept, because people hear my people and think it means all nations.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
I will cause the remnant of this people to possess all these things. The remnant that possesses them is named in the prophets. “For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return: the consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness.”

The remnant is of thy people Israel. This is why the bible must be read precept upon precept: people hear my people and think it means all nations, but the remnant that returns and possesses the prosperous seed, the fruit of the vine and the increase of the ground is the children of Israel.

moments.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

points: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees. Woe, meaning destruction, unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, meaning unrighteous laws against the people, for the destruction of the people, the destruction of the land. Because that is what is happening in all these countries when you take those precious minerals out of the earth. This is why the tectonic plates move, earthquakes happen. You are not supposed to remove the minerals. These minerals are in the earth for a reason.
And that write grievousness which they have prescribed. They prescribe evil, prescribed grievousness to our people.

To turn aside the needy from judgment. They move our people out of the way. We are going to get this land by any means necessary. Move. If you do not move with the unrighteous decree, then we come with force. What was it that John Perkins used to say? First they send the economic hit man. If you do not accept the deal by the economic hit man, they send the jackals. And if the jackals cannot take you out, they send the US military. That is how it goes.
And to take away the right from the poor of my people. To take away the rights of the rightful owners of the land, the rightful owners of the country.

That widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless. Widows are their prey. We have seen videos, and we are going to show more videos, where they are attacking our people, killing the widows, taking the children from their parents. They may rob us, the fatherless, of our lands, displace us, terrorize us. All this is by design.
Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees and write grievousness.
Only those with power to pass laws against a whole people can be called oppressors in this sense.
Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees to turn aside the needy from judgment.
They take away the right of the poor, the right to their oil and land, and make widows their prey.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

points: Woe is pronounced on those who decree unrighteous decrees and write grievous laws to turn aside the needy from judgment and take away the right from the poor. That is us: we are the needy, we are the poor.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The unrighteous decrees rob the widows and the fatherless. The question is put to the oppressor: what will you do in the day of visitation and desolation, to whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glory. Without the Most High they bow down under the prisoners and fall under the slain, for His anger is not turned away and His hand is stretched out still.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The Most High calls the Assyrian the rod of His anger, the staff in their hand His indignation. He used nations to punish us. He sends the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, the people of His wrath, to take the spoil and tread them down like the mire of the streets.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The Assyrian did not mean it that way; it was in his heart to destroy and cut off nations. He boasted of the kingdoms he conquered and their idols, not realizing the Most High was using him to punish us and the rest of the nations. We had graven images throughout our land, breaking the Most High's laws.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: When the Most High has finished His work on Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Assyrian said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent," boasting that he removed the treasures and inhabitants of the people on his own.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The Most High asks whether the axe boasts against the one who hews with it, or the saw magnifies itself against the one who shakes it. The Assyrian was only the axe; the Most High used him to cut us down from rulership to captivity.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: Therefore the Most High sends leanness among the fat ones and kindles a burning fire that devours the thorns and briers in one day and consumes the glory of the forest, both soul and body, until the trees are so few a child may write them.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: In that day the remnant of Israel and those who escaped of the house of Jacob shall no more stay upon him that smote them, but stay upon the Most High, the Holy One of Israel, in truth. This is a future prophecy.

"Stay" means to rely upon. Just like back then, we still rely upon the ones who smote us, even today under the nation of Edom, trusting in oppression, relying on the very ones still smiting us in the streets. In that day the remnant, those keeping the Most High's commandments in their right mind, will escape and stop leaning on the oppressor.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: Though Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. The Most High will make a consumption decreed and overflowing with righteousness in the midst of all the land.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The Most High tells His people who dwell in Zion not to be afraid of the Assyrian who smites with a rod and lifts up his staff after the manner of Egypt, for in a very little while the indignation will cease and His anger will turn to their destruction.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The Most High will stir up a scourge for the Assyrian, and his yoke shall be taken off Israel's neck and destroyed because of the anointing.

note.label: Isaiah 10: Woe to the Oppressor and the Remnant That Escapes

points: The chapter traces the invader's march through the towns until he shakes his hand against the mount of the daughter of Zion. Then the Most High of hosts lops the bough with terror, the high ones are hewn down, and Lebanon falls by a mighty one.
